rv.q: But these conflicts aren't enough to inject real dramatic momentum into Nelson's slow-moving production.
Nelson’s vision of the Roosevelt family’s Springwood estate in upstate New York is an intimate one, with the thrust staging inserting us directly into their living room.
It's well performed by a stellar cast who do their best with what they are given. But what they are given is a stodgy pudding rather than a sizzling hot dog.
This play should have been a resounding success. That is not to say it is a failure by any stretch - it just struggles to reach its full potential.

cn.t: A historically intriguing but dramatically inert account of FDR's 1939 royal visit receives lukewarm reviews, with critics finding the material static and underdeveloped despite its fascinating premise.
